text: Stay right where you are. Eyes can stay closed.
Give me ten minutes before the world gets you.
Couple of breaths first. Then we go.
Breathe in through your nose... and then a little more on top.
Now let it all out, slow, through your mouth.
One more like that. In... a little more on top... and long and slow out.
Good. Now let's wake the body up.
In for four... two... three... four... Out for four... two... three... four.
In... two... three... four... Out... two... three... four.
In... two... three... four... Out... two... three... four.
Last one. Big. In... two... three... four... Out... two... three... four.
If you can, sit up. Let your back get tall.
There it is. Same calm you practiced last night.
Now picture a dial in the middle of your chest. Right now it's set to "sleepy."
Calm body. Curious mind. Clear voice.
Nobody's coming to save the conversation. I steer it. With a question.
I don't chase. I ask, and they walk toward it.
Overthinking is importance turned up too high. I turn it down. I ask the next question.
I don't need the perfect line. I need the next question.
Thinking poor is explaining yourself to strangers. Thinking rich is asking what they need.
I let silence do the closing.
My numbers are clean. I say the price once, like the weather. Then I shut up.
One conversation. One lane. One next step.
I don't do guilt. I don't do fake deadlines. I don't do made-up proof. I don't need to.
A "no" is information. I ask what would have to change, and I move on clean.
I'd be fine if they could hear my thoughts. That's why they trust me.
The lot. A buyer walks up, guarded. Thumb to finger. One breath.
"What's going on with the one you've got?"
He tells you. You say it back in one line. The price comes out clean. Then: "Want to drive it now, or after lunch?"
An owner's office. Skeptical. Phone buzzing.
"What happens to a message that comes in at nine at night?"
"How many of those go cold in a week?"
He does his math. You say the price once. You stop talking.
An investor. Sharp. Seen it all. Your numbers are exact.
"What would make this a clear yes for you?"
"What worries you most about me, honestly?"
You answer it straight. Terms once, clean. Quiet. You're fine either way, and she can feel it.
A conference room. One talks. One decides.
"Tuesday at ten, or Thursday after lunch?"
An interview. They ask. You answer straight, real numbers.
Then: "What would make the person in this seat a clear win in ninety days?"
"Is there anything about my background that gives you pause?"
Now pick the one conversation today that matters most.
What's the first question you'll ask them?
Good. When you walk in, that's the first thing out of your mouth.
When I feel the urge to explain... I ask.
When they hit me with three questions... I answer one, clean, and ask one back.
When they say it's too much... I ask what they're comparing it to.
When it goes quiet after my question... I count to five in my head, and I let it work.
In a moment I'll count from one to five. On five, your eyes open and you're all the way awake.
One. Feel your feet. Wiggle your toes.
Two. The breath gets bigger. Fill your chest.
Three. Blood moving in your hands. Make a fist and let it go.
Four. Your eyes getting bright behind the lids. Clear head.
Five. Eyes open. Wide awake. Clear. Ready.
Thumb to finger, one time, eyes open. Ask.
That's it. That's the whole game today.
Ask first. Let them say it. Say the number clean. One next step.
